chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Aban ibn Taghlib who said:

I went out with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) between Mecca and Medina, and he would say, 'As for you, you are young men who delay [prayer], and as for me, I am an old man who hurries [prayer].' So he would pray the night prayer at the beginning of the night.

key_terms.أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ: Aban ibn Taghlib, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ: At the beginning of the night

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam pray the night prayer early during his travels?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the spiritual capacity of youth, who can delay night prayers, and his own status as an elder anticipating death, who hastens to pray. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the timing of *Salat al-Layl* is flexible and tied to individual readiness and the urgency of the Hereafter. It serves as a practical guide for balancing rigorous devotion with the physical realities of aging.
